value.rationale: The question of how a geometric probability depends on the intrinsic sampling measure is classically motivated. The explicit second-variation coefficient shows a sharp reversal at exactly Euclidean arclength: increasing anisotropy initially decreases acuteness below this exponent and increases it above. The cancellation is not a rescaling or parameter substitution of a known exact law; it compares genuinely distinct sampling geometries. The result identifies the uniquely quadratic-neutral density among natural speed-power sampling laws.
